decisions.reason: The accepted change governs mint-success modal variants, timing, and retry feedback; it does not necessarily revise the separate FAQ content.
Mint-result copy and random-finalization feedback do not change which NFT properties or active tickets follow an NFT transfer.
The source concerns referral-specific mint-success feedback and does not alter gratuity selection, payment, or delayed-tip notices.
The accepted modal behavior does not require any change to landing-page copy or layout.
The source changes how pending or failed random commission finalization is communicated, not the $12 no-referral commission amount, trigger, recipient selection, or coverage.
The source changes success-modal timing and retry feedback but does not alter no-referral ticket quantity, eligibility, or weighted allocation.
The accepted feedback behavior is independent of the deferred Transak provider, wallet provisioning, and fiat-mint flow.
The source repeats a $12 commission in modal copy but does not change the mint price or allocation among founder, affiliate, and prize pool.
The coded-referral modal uses the already-current $12 commission and does not change its amount, recipient, payout destination, or eligibility rules.
Mint-success copy, prompt visibility, and finalization-failure feedback do not change NFT metadata fields or their source of truth.
The source governs post-mint result feedback across referral scenarios and does not change the ability to complete a connected-wallet USDC mint.
The accepted feedback changes do not affect the NFT ebook format or unlimited edition supply.
